plans.evaluator_notes:
No dollar price estimates are stored in this file. Enter allowed prices in the evaluator's section 2 (Costs).
ER, imaging (CT/MRI), outpatient surgery and hospital stays are flat copays that apply after the deductible; the evaluator needs a full allowed price for them (section 2) to count the deductible correctly.
Ultrasound uses the plan's x-ray and diagnostic imaging cost share ($30 copay).

extraction.assumptions:
Deductible applies = true for hospital, delivery facility, mental health inpatient, inpatient rehabilitation and habilitation, and skilled nursing: they are not on the plan page's list of services covered before the deductible.
Deductible applies = true for durable medical equipment for the same reason.
The primary care price equals every sick visit ($15); an annual preventive visit is no charge.
extraction.notes:
Tier 3 and Tier 4 drugs are coinsurance with no dollar price in the documents.
The SBC does not state whether the deductible applies to lab and x-ray at other places of service ($350 copay), so it is left unset.
Mail order is 90 days at 2.5x the retail copay for Tier 1 and Tier 2; Tier 4 is 30 days.
SBC coverage examples are self-only coverage.

plans.evaluator_notes:
No dollar price estimates are stored in this file. Every service except visits, home health, hospice and Tier 1 drugs is 40% coinsurance after the deductible, so the documents give no dollar price; enter allowed prices in the evaluator's section 2 (Costs).
Ultrasound uses the plan's x-ray and diagnostic imaging cost share (40% after the deductible).

extraction.assumptions:
Deductible applies = true for emergency transportation, hospital, delivery, inpatient and other outpatient mental health, rehabilitation, habilitation, skilled nursing and durable medical equipment: they are not on the plan page's list of services covered before the deductible.
The '$1 for the first two visits' rule is recorded on primary care, outpatient mental health office visits and chiropractic. The plan page says the two visits cover primary care, chiropractic, hearing exams and MH/SUD together, so the real total across all of them is two; the evaluator counts the primary care discount only.
extraction.notes:
The plan page says HSA eligible: Yes. The plan type is HMO, and the out-of-pocket maximum ($23,600 family) is above the usual HDHP cap, so the evaluator may show an HDHP warning; confirm eligibility with the carrier.
Drug tiers 2 to 4 are 40% coinsurance with no dollar price in the documents.
Mail order is 90 days at 2.5x the retail copay for Tier 1 and Tier 2; Tier 4 is 30 days.
SBC coverage examples are self-only coverage.
